newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Semicon up on ex-bonus issue date.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Semicon up on ex-bonus issue date.

text.p: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co, Taiwan's top chipmaker, surged at mid-morning on Thursday, the date it went ex-bonus issue, brokers said.
The company on Thursday issued a stock dividend, or bonus issue of T$5 per share for 1996, or 500 shares free for every 1,000 shares held.
After 75 minutes, at 0215 GMT, Taiwan Semiconductor rose the daily seven percent limit to T$91, while the overall index fell 1.02 percent.
Brokers attributed the buying to the firm's sound outlook.

"The outlook for the semiconductor industry, especially the leader Taiwan Semiconductor, is very good," said independent analyst Michael Hung. "The semiconductor industry is just bottoming-out, and its recovery usually will last for a period of two to three years," Hung said.
Taiwan Semiconductor likely will rise consecutively in the coming sessions to around T$110, Hung said.

In April, Taiwan Semiconductor said it would invest T$400 billion at southern Taiwan's Tainan science-based industrial park over the next 10 years. It would be Taiwan's largest single industrial project. -- Taipei Newsroom (5080815)
